questions.question_text: What is the exact value of $e^{\ln 12}$?

options.why: took the reciprocal of the argument instead of applying the inverse identity
raised $e$ to the argument instead of simplifying the inverse composition
confused $e^{\ln x}$ with $e^0 = 1$

questions.solution_text:
Because exponential and natural logarithm are inverse functions, $e^{\ln x} = x$ for all $x>0$.
$e^{\ln 12} = 12$

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is mathematically correct for all positive real numbers $a$ and $b$?

options.why: applied the false logarithm law expanding across a sum
confused a ratio of logarithms with the logarithm of a difference
placed the power outside the logarithm instead of bringing it down as a factor $k\ln a$

questions.solution_text: The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the individual logarithms: $\ln(ab) = \ln a + \ln b$.
